security_spec.violation_condition: If XiangShan's integer multiplier (execution unit for MUL) implements early-termination or operand-dependent-latency optimization (e.g., Booth-encoding skip on zero operands, short-circuit on small multiplicands), then c.mul—being Zkt-listed—must execute with data-independent latency. Any microarchitectural timing variation observable via rd-vs-rs1/rs2 operand patterns violates the Zkt constant-time guarantee, even when c.mul expands to the same 32-bit mul datapath. Similarly, if the decoder inserts different pipeline bubbles or selects different functional-unit dispatch paths for compressed vs. uncompressed encodings, c.not (xori rd, rs, -1) and c.zext.b (andi rd, rs, 0xFF) could exhibit Zcb-specific timing signatures not present for the base I-instruction equivalents.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: MUL_early_termination OR Booth_skip_zero_operand OR compressed_instruction_dispatch_bubble OR Zcb_expansion_delay_cycle OR data_dependent_mul_latency OR operand_gated_multiplier_stages
security_spec.summary: Zcb compressed instructions c.mul/c.not/c.zext.b must inherit Zkt constant-time guarantees in hardware; any data-dependent timing in multiplier or ALU datapath (including compressed-expansion pipeline bubbles) leaks operand information via execution-latency side channel
